\section[il cerotto]{il cerotto — a plaster}

\label{lesson:IT-C243-cerotto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to collect, then the Italian for to turn to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il cerotto}
\textbf{il cerotto} — \textquotedblleft{}a plaster\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{cerotto} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{cerotum}, \textquotedblleft{}a wax plaster\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{keros}, \textquotedblleft{}beeswax\textquotedblright{} — inherited. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}

\section[l'ambulanza]{l'ambulanza — an ambulance}

\label{lesson:IT-C243-ambulanza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to turn to, then the Italian for a plaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'ambulanza}
\textbf{l'ambulanza} — \textquotedblleft{}an ambulance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{ambulanza} $\leftarrow$ French \emph{ambulance} — borrowed. EtymDB 2.1 has no row for \emph{ambulanza}; it builds the French word on \emph{ambulant}, \textquotedblleft{}walking\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{ambulare}, \textquotedblleft{}to walk\textquotedblright{}: a field hospital that moved.
\end{cousinweb}
